thread:
maria: Heads-up — since the kernel-selection tweak yesterday we've seen a small but consistent uptick in OOMs on long-context jobs (L=32k). Not many, but p99 OOM rate went from 0.04% -> 0.6% on dedicated pool A. Suspect buffer fragmentation + workspace sizing.

devon: Interesting. Did this correlate with batching changes too? We changed the batching heuristic for dynamic batching to prefer larger batches at higher concurrency. Could be larger contiguous allocations exposing slab fragmentation.

maria: Good call. Timeline: kernel selection change (better matmul path for short seqs) rolled at 09:12, batching heuristic change at 09:17. OOMs started ~09:30. KV cache fill for some tenants spiked at same time (more long-context requests).

jon: I pulled a heap/profile from one of the crashed workers. Attaching key bits.

profile-bot: ```
GPU malloc peaks: 40.7GB
Allocated tensors (count): activations 312, logits 24, scratchpad 48
Top alloc sizes: activation slabs ~128k chunks (many small), logits buffers ~2MB each
Free list fragmentation: 12 gaps >4MB
KV cache reserved: 8GB
Workspace requested vs granted (p95): 9.8GB vs 7.2GB (fallback to allocating extra pages)
OOM trace: allocation request 5.6GB failed after many small frees
```

maria: The key is logits + scratchpad reuse. Right now we create logits buffers per generation step for multi-token streaming and free them fast. That churn plus freelist fragmentation seems to prevent a 5–6GB contiguous allocation when workspace scales up for a long KV-augmented request.

amber: Do we have a quick mitigation we can canary? Suggested options:
- reserve a large preallocated logits slab per worker and sub-allocate (less fragmentation)
- switch logits buffers to pooled reuse (per-thread freelist with cacheline-aligned blocks)
- force compaction by evicting small cached KV pages (risky)

devon: I prototyped a per-worker logits slab and a tiny change to allocator metadata to mark logits allocations as "sticky" so they prefer the logits slab. Quick bench on devbox: memory high-water dropped 6.2GB -> 3.1GB for a synthetic 32k stream workload. p50 latency +1.8%, p99 +3.5% (within SLO currently).

benchbot: Canary bench (simulated 10 tenants, 30s steady):
- baseline (no slab): p99 latency 214ms, throughput 190 rps, OOMs 0.5%
- logits-slab: p99 222ms, throughput 188 rps, OOMs 0.0%
Memory HWM: baseline 41.1GB, slab 36.0GB

jon: Those numbers look promising. We need to double-check interactions with KV cache eviction policies — preallocating a logits slab reduces available contiguous space for workspace growth. But it also reduces fragmentation so net win here. We should test worst-case where KV grows to 12GB.

maria: Proposed plan for canary rollout:
1) Enable `runtime.pool.logits_slab.enabled = true` and `runtime.pool.logits_slab.size_mb = 4096` on 10% of Dedicated pool (canary tag)
2) Add infra metric: logits_slab_utilization, alloc_fail_contig, free_frag_percent
3) Monitor OOM count, p99 latency, and KV eviction rate for 2h
4) Revert if alloc_fail_contig increases or OOMs don't drop within 30m

devon: Implementation notes (pseudo):
```
// on worker init
logits_slab = slab_alloc(logits_slab_size);
// allocation path
if (type == LOGITS && slab_has_room(size)) return slab_suballoc(size);
else return general_alloc(size);
```
Also added a fast-path free that pushes freed logits blocks back to a per-worker ring cache to avoid touching central freelist frequently.

amber: Also add a conservative fallback to allocate from general pool if slab is full, to avoid hard failures. And emit a metric when fallback occurs.

maria: Agreed. Jon, can you add workload with KV growth to the perf suite and run overnight with the slab variant? Want regressions under heavy KV + long streams.

jon: On it. I'll run two passes: (A) KV steady 8GB (B) KV spike to 12GB while streaming 32k. I'll attach logs in the morning.

profile-bot: Quick follow-up: we should also tune scratchpad sizing (currently 64MB default per-thread). For large attention windows scratchpad usage can balloon; consider adaptive scratchpad that shrinks when logits_slab_util < 20% to avoid double-reserving.

devon: Good idea — add `scratchpad.adaptive = true` with min/max caps. Minor change in allocator but could avoid double-counting reserved regions.

maria: OK timeline: devon lands logits_slab PR with fallback + metrics today, jon runs KV stress overnight, amber prepares canary group and dashboards. If overnight pass looks clean, enable canary at 10% tomorrow morning.

amber: I'll add alert: `oom_rate > 0.3% over 30m` for canary group. Also `alloc_fail_contig > 5` -> page us.

maria: Thanks all. If anyone has simpler immediate mitigation (e.g., reduce batching heuristic aggressiveness) we can flip that too while tests run.

devon: I'll leave batching heuristic rollback as an escape hatch — flag name `batching.dynamic.large_batch_bias` set to 0.0 to disable the large-batch bias.

maria: Perfect. Keep updates here.
